title: How should 3, 5 and 9 fill the frame for the largest answer?
description: The digits three, five and nine fill a frame of two boxes times one box. The largest digit becomes the multiplier, the other two go in decreasing order, and place value gives the answer. The next best way is checked and found smaller.
teaching_notes: One idea: the largest digit is the multiplier and the other two digits go in decreasing order in the two digit number. Watch for students who put the largest digit in the tens place of the two digit number.

source: Figure it Out (the largest product, question 2)
video_script.why: The child uses the rule from the solved example: the largest digit multiplies and the others go in decreasing order.
video_script.substitution: Digits 3, 5 and 9: multiplier 9, two digit number 53, multiply by place value, then check the next best way.
video_script.anchor: the frame of two boxes, a times sign and one box, with the digits 3, 5 and 9 to place
video_script.payoff_line: The largest answer is fifty three times nine, which is four hundred seventy seven

final_answer.spoken: fifty three times nine, which is four hundred seventy seven

maths_rules: largest digit 9 is the multiplier; the other digits 5 and 3 in decreasing order give 53
video_script.design: One idea: the largest digit is the multiplier. The frame stays on the board all video and the check is the last step.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='cards'/>Fill the digits three, five and nine into a two digit number times a one digit number.
<bookmark mark='frame'/>The frame has two boxes, the times sign and one box.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Which way gives the largest multiplication answer?

beats.on_screen: the cards and the frame stay on the board while the child thinks

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: arrows run from the one digit box to both boxes of the two digit number

marks.plan: the frame is shown again with the three cards beside it
marks.both: arrows run from the single box to both digits of the two digit number

narration: <bookmark mark='plan'/>We solve it the same way as the example in your book.
<bookmark mark='both'/>The one digit multiplier works on both digits of the two digit number. The digit we choose to multiply matters a lot.

beats.on_screen: Given: digits 3, 5, 9, each used once, in (two digit) × (one digit)

marks.given: the digits and the frame are written on the board

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the digits three, five and nine, each used once. They fill a two digit number times a one digit number.

beats.on_screen: To find: the largest multiplication answer

marks.find: the words largest multiplication answer are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the largest multiplication answer.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: the largest digit 9 is the multiplier

marks.nine: the card 9 moves into the single box

beats.colours: the multiplier in the accent colour
narration: <bookmark mark='nine'/>Step one, take the largest digit, nine, as the multiplier. It works on both digits of the other number.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: the other digits in decreasing order: 5 then 3, so 53 × 9

marks.five: the card 5 moves into the tens box
marks.three: the card 3 moves into the ones box

narration: <bookmark mark='five'/>Step two, put the other two digits in decreasing order, five first.
<bookmark mark='three'/>That makes the two digit number fifty three.

marks.values: 450 and 27 are written under the two parts

narration: <bookmark mark='split'/>Step three, multiply by place value. Fifty times nine is four hundred fifty.
<bookmark mark='values'/>Three times nine is twenty seven, and the two parts are added.

beats.on_screen: Step 4, check the next best way: 93 × 5 = (90 × 5) + (3 × 5) = 450 + 15 = 465; 465 is less than 53 × 9
narration: <bookmark mark='next'/>Step four, check the next best way, ninety three times five. Ninety times five is four hundred fifty, and three times five is fifteen.
<bookmark mark='less'/>That gives four hundred sixty five, which is smaller.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The largest answer is fifty three times nine, which is four hundred seventy seven.
